$comment: LW-WATCHTOWER module switchboard. Claude Code has no per-hook disable - disableAllHooks is all-or-nothing and would also kill the status line - so every module gates itself on the flags below. Edit this file; no reinstall is needed because the plugin is loaded through a directory junction.

$status.$comment: READ THIS BEFORE THE FLAGS BELOW. A flag set to true is a forward-declaration of intent, NOT evidence that any code exists. Anything listed under "planned" would be a name with no behaviour behind it, and switching such a name on or off changes nothing. "planned" is EMPTY as of 30 July 2026 - every flag in the `modules` block is backed by code and enabled, and so are the three gates, which are backed by code and switched OFF - and the rule stands anyway, because it is the rule that keeps the count honest the next time a name is added ahead of its code. THERE IS ONE AUTHORITATIVE LIST AND IT IS NOT IN THIS FILE: $LwgModuleRegistry in lib/common.ps1. The SessionStart banner reads it, bin/lwg-doctor.ps1's config-registry check holds the `modules` block below to it, and Get-LwgImplementedModules answers 'which modules are built' from it for anything that asks.
$status.$removed_implemented_comment: AN "implemented" ARRAY USED TO SIT ON THIS LINE, naming every module in the registry a second time, and it was DELETED ON 3 SEPTEMBER 2026 (#75) rather than wired to a check. The removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence. NOTHING IN THE TREE EVER READ IT - not bin/lwg-doctor.ps1's config-registry check, which compares the `modules` keys against $LwgModuleRegistry and the declared switch keys and never looked at this array; not any rule in tests/doc_claims.ps1; not any hook - while the comment beside it told the next reader that a machine was keeping the array and the `modules` block in step. A hand-maintained copy of the registry, believed because a comment named a machine that does not exist, is a stale list wearing the authority of a checked one: add a module, forget this array, and CI stays green while the file quietly reports one fewer module than exists. That is the shape this plugin exists to catch - a switch wired to nothing - so the copy went instead of gaining a check nobody asked for. What the array's own comment was RIGHT about is kept, because it is a real property of the `modules` block: four modules - delegate_gate, send_liveness_gate, completion_audit and orphan_watch - are deliberately absent from it, because each declares its own switch (interaction.delegate for the first; the `supervision` block further down for the other three) on its registry entry via the `switch` field. Two flags over one module would let an operator turn it on with a command and have it silently do nothing, and Get-LwgConfig fails OPEN - a corrupt config must never arm a blocking gate.
$status.$planned_comment: EMPTY, and that is now the honest answer: every name in the `modules` block below is backed by code. It used to hold ratelimit_escalation and cost_tracking; both were removed on 30 July 2026 at the owner's instruction - see $removed_blocked_comment. The key is kept rather than deleted so that a future unbuilt module has somewhere to be declared without inventing the convention again.
$status.$default_off_comment: EMPTY, and it stays empty because this key only ever described the `modules` block below - every one of those seven is built and enabled. THE REGISTRY IS NO LONGER ALL-ENABLED, and that is not a contradiction: FOUR modules ship built and switched OFF - delegate_gate (flag interaction.delegate) and the three supervision modules send_liveness_gate, completion_audit and orphan_watch (flags in the `supervision` block) - and none of their flags is a `modules` key, so none is a member of the list this one is about. They are named here anyway, because 'default_off is empty' would otherwise read as 'nothing ships off', which is not true.
$status.$self_health_comment: self_health honours its flag. Set it to false and the SessionStart self-check does not run at all - no probe, no config-parsed assertion, no state-dir write test. The banner and the model-visible context then report mode 'unverified' and say in words that nothing was checked. They deliberately do NOT say 'enforcing', 'partial' or 'observe-only': those three all assert that the self-check passed, and asserting that on the strength of a check that never ran is the same lie as counting an unbuilt module as coverage. 'degraded' would be the opposite lie - it claims a probe failed, and none did.
$status.$context_injection_comment: context_injection is the SubagentStart hook (lib/subagent_start.ps1). Claude Code snapshots CLAUDE.md into a subagent's context at PARENT-SESSION start, so an instruction added mid-session never reaches a worker dispatched later - a security classifier here once refused a legitimate edit because its snapshot predated the instruction authorising it. SubagentStart fires per dispatch, so what it emits is always current. It injects context/worker_facts.md as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, reading that file live every time; edit the file and the next dispatch picks it up with no code change. Facts only, under 80 words - every dispatch pays for the text. Set this to false and the hook emits nothing and exits 0.
$status.$removed_blocked_comment: ratelimit_escalation and cost_tracking WERE declared here as 'planned'. Both were REMOVED ON 30 JULY 2026 by an explicit owner decision, and the removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence: a name that can never be built is not a plan, and carrying it in a switchboard invites someone to switch it on. THE REASON THEY CANNOT BE BUILT IS NOT DELETED WITH THEM - it lives in docs/modules.md under 'Attempted and blocked: ratelimit_escalation and cost_tracking', in full, with the field-by-field evidence, so that nobody re-attempts them. In one line: verified against the claude-code 2.1.220 binary, rate_limits / cost / context_window / workspace are assembled in exactly ONE place, the status-line input builder, and no hook event carries any of them. DO NOT ADD EITHER NAME BACK to the modules block below without first reading that section; a flag with no reachable data behind it is the precise defect this plugin exists to catch. The status line already colours rate-limit usage and prints its 'land all work' advisory, because that is the one process that receives the data - see thresholds.ratelimit below.
$status.$gates_comment: THREE GATES SHIP AND ALL THREE ARE OFF. A `gates_live` integer used to sit above this line asserting that; it was DELETED because nothing computed it, nothing validated it and nothing updated it - it went false inside this very file the moment an operator set interaction.delegate to true, which is the one supported way to arm a gate. Get-LwgActiveGates answers the live count from the registry and the switches, correctly, for anything that asks. The LIVE / SHIPPED distinction the number tried to carry is still the whole point: delegate_gate (PreToolUse on Edit|Write|NotebookEdit|Bash, switch interaction.delegate), send_liveness_gate (PreToolUse on SendMessage, switch supervision.send_liveness) and completion_audit (a Stop entry with no asyncRewake, switch supervision.completion_audit) are each declared in $LwgModuleRegistry with kind 'gate', each registered in hooks/hooks.json, and each blocks nothing at all until its own switch is set to true. Turn one on and the count rises, Get-LwgActiveGates returns it, and the session mode leaves 'observe-only' - all of that follows from the registry fields with no other edit. Every OTHER module is kind 'observe': it reports, logs or advises, and the action happens regardless. HISTORY: destructive_gate and then secret_scan were removed on 30 July 2026 at the owner's instruction, leaving no gate of any kind; delegate_gate was built later the same day as the one gate then fully buildable, and send_liveness_gate + completion_audit were built 1 August 2026 from the measured queued-message-reported-as-done failure recorded in the `supervision` block's $comment. THE TRIP LEDGER DID NOT COME BACK WITH ANY OF THEM - a denial is recorded in lw-watchtower.jsonl as a GateDeny event and nothing tracks it as an open item. Read docs/gates-removed.md before adding another gate - it records why the first two went, what the four failed fix attempts taught, and the rules a new gate has to follow; the two new gates, like delegate_gate, parse no shell and decide nothing about whether content is safe.
$status.$removed_comment: destructive_gate WAS the second live gate - a PreToolUse hook on Bash|PowerShell (lib/gate_bash.ps1) refusing force pushes, hard resets, history rewrites, recursive deletes and GitHub repo destruction, plus a path half in the since-deleted lib/gate_write.ps1 refusing writes inside a .git directory. It was REMOVED ON 30 JULY 2026 by an explicit owner decision, and the removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence. NOTHING in this plugin inspects a shell command any more, and no write to .git internals is refused by any hook. The permissions.deny mirror went in the same change: bin/lwg-setup.ps1 dropped the git-destructive, filesystem-destructive, github-destructive and git-internals groups (133 of 181 rules), so a fresh install has neither a hook layer nor a config layer for destructive commands. A machine set up before that date still carries the old rules in its own settings.json and the CLI still evaluates them; nothing here renews them. The code is recoverable from git history; see CHANGELOG.md for the commits.
$status.$removed_secret_comment: secret_scan WAS the last gate, and it was REMOVED ON 30 JULY 2026 by an explicit owner decision, in the same spirit as the destructive gate above and recorded here rather than left to be inferred. It was a PreToolUse hook on Write|Edit|NotebookEdit (lib/gate_write.ps1, now DELETED) that refused writes to credential paths - *.pem, *.key, id_rsa*, .env and friends - and writes whose CONTENT carried a live GitHub, AWS or Slack token. Both halves are gone: no hook inspects the path being written and no hook inspects the bytes being written. Its permissions.deny mirror went in the same change - bin/lwg-setup.ps1 dropped the secret-paths and secret-reads groups, the last 48 of the original 181 rules - so the deny table the installer writes is now EMPTY and a fresh install has neither a hook layer nor a config layer for credentials. Nothing this plugin ships can stop a secret reaching disk. A machine set up before that date still carries the 48 rules in its own settings.json unless they were removed by hand; nothing here renews them. THE TRIP LEDGER WENT THE SAME DAY, AFTER THE GATES: lib/trips.ps1, lib/ack_trip.ps1, bin/lwg-tripped.ps1 and commands/tripped.md were kept for a few hours as readers for the per-session ledgers already on disk, and were then removed with those ledgers by a further explicit owner decision. The ledger files were backed up before deletion, not destroyed. Nothing now records, reads, closes or acknowledges a trip, and a future gate has to rebuild the whole format - see docs/gates-removed.md. The code is recoverable from git history; see CHANGELOG.md for the commits.

interaction.$comment: INTERACTION PREFERENCES. ONE KEY IS LEFT: `delegate`. It is absent from the `modules` block above for the same reason `output_style` is - a corrupt config must not be able to flip it, because Get-LwgConfig fails OPEN and would switch on a blocking gate nobody asked for - but it is NOT merely a preference any more. Since 30 July 2026 it is the switch on delegate_gate, a real PreToolUse gate, and $LwgModuleRegistry in lib/common.ps1 carries a `delegate_gate` entry whose `switch` field names this exact key. That is why there is no second flag for it in `modules`: two switches over one gate lets an operator turn it on with the command and have it silently do nothing, which is the founding defect this plugin exists to catch. bin/lwg-doctor.ps1's config-registry check asserts that this key is present here and that the registry entry points at it.
interaction.$removed_keys_comment: `ask` and `ask_inline` WERE HERE, defaulting to true, and both were REMOVED ON 30 JULY 2026 by an explicit owner decision. The removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence, because both had been ON by default since they shipped while enforcing nothing at all. Neither can be built as specified: `ask` would need a Stop hook refusing to end a turn while an unanswered decision is outstanding, and a Stop hook can block turn-end but cannot stop prose from having already appeared and cannot detect a question that should have been asked and was not - so the half that matters is unreachable. `ask_inline` would need something that counts and merges the questions asked in a turn, and nothing can merge them after the fact; the 4-questions / 2-4-options shape was always a platform limit on the question tool rather than a rule this plugin applied. commands/ask.md and commands/ask-inline.md are deleted, bin/lwg-toggle.ps1 no longer accepts either name, and a flag left here would be a setting nothing reads. DO NOT ADD EITHER KEY BACK without a mechanism, not a hook name.
interaction.$delegate_comment: DEFAULT FALSE, AND IT SHIPS FALSE ON PURPOSE. Its on state changes how work is done without being asked, and shipping a blocking gate switched on by default is the opposite of what this plugin argues for everywhere else. Set it true - /lw-watchtower:delegate on - and lib/gate_delegate.ps1 refuses Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash and PowerShell for any call that did not come from a subagent. PowerShell joined that list on 1 August 2026: this is a Windows-only plugin, the CLI offers both shell tools there, and the matcher named only one of them - so an armed gate could be walked round by asking for the other shell while /lw-watchtower:doctor reported it live. WHAT THAT COSTS, stated here rather than discovered: /lw-watchtower:delegate off will not work from the main thread afterwards, because that command runs its script through Bash and Bash is one of the five. There is deliberately no exemption for it. The two ways back are to have a subagent run the command, or to set this key to false by hand. An unreadable config leaves the gate OFF rather than on, which is the polarity that keeps a bad config a nuisance instead of a lockout.
interaction.$repo_override_comment: Per-repo overrides live under `repos` below, in a block of the same name and alongside `modules`: "repos": { "LEAPWare-Software/example-repo": { "interaction": { "delegate": true } } }. Only the keys listed under a repo are overridden; everything else falls through to the default here. /lw-watchtower:delegate on repo writes that entry and creates the repo object if it is absent, and lib/gate_delegate.ps1 honours it - the gate resolves its switch through the same Test-LwgModule the banner uses, so a per-repo override applies to the gate exactly as it applies to a module.

supervision.$comment: COMPLETION-INTEGRITY MODULES, ALL THREE OFF BY DEFAULT, built 1 August 2026 from a measured failure: an orchestrator issued SendMessage to a subagent that had been DEAD FOR 28 MINUTES 45 SECONDS, read the 'Message queued for delivery' acknowledgement as done, and told the user 3.46 seconds later that a file had been updated which was never touched - while the health log read green, because Get-FailedTasks counts only failed/killed BACKGROUND TASKS and a subagent killed mid-flight produces no record anywhere (a cross-check found FOUR such orphans, against a log with zero PostToolUseFailure records in 1,175 entries). The keys live HERE and not in the `modules` block for the same reason interaction.delegate does: Get-LwgConfig fails OPEN, and a corrupt config must never arm a blocking gate nobody asked for. Each key is declared on its own registry entry in lib/common.ps1 via the `switch` field, bin/lwg-doctor.ps1 asserts the declared keys exist, and per-repo overrides go under `repos` exactly as for delegate: "repos": { "Owner/Name": { "supervision": { "send_liveness": true } } }.
supervision.$send_liveness_comment: send_liveness_gate (lib/gate_send.ps1), PreToolUse on SendMessage. ON: refuses a send whose recipient it can prove is dead mid-flight - transcript exists for this session, no SubagentStop record, transcript silent past module_config.send_liveness_gate.stale_minutes - and refuses a recipient that resolves to nothing at all. Abstains (allows, logged) on `name@team` addresses and on sessions health.jsonl never recorded. DO NOT ARM THIS in an agent-team workflow; it does not understand team layouts and will refuse bare teammate names it cannot resolve.
supervision.$completion_audit_comment: completion_audit (lib/gate_stop.ps1), a Stop entry registered WITHOUT asyncRewake, so its exit 2 BLOCKS the turn end. ON: refuses to end a turn whose final assistant text asserts completed work while the turn's last tool action was SendMessage - queued is not delivered, delivered is not done. Fires at most once per turn end (stop_hook_active stands it down on the continuation), so it forces one round of verification and cannot force honesty. Its claim detection is a stated regex over prose; read the false-positive/negative enumeration in lib/gate_stop.ps1 before arming it.
supervision.$orphan_watch_comment: orphan_watch (inside lib/supervisor.ps1, run from BOTH the Stop and the SubagentStop branches - Stop alone proved far too sparse a trigger, costing a measured 42-minute detection delay on 10 August 2026 while three SubagentStop events fired unused; and it reads the harness's OWN task-notification for a stated cause, which is believed with no threshold at all). ON: reconciles this session's subagent transcripts against its SubagentStop records and alerts - through the supervisor's existing exit-2 asyncRewake path, deduped per agent via alerted.json - on any agent the parent transcript records as <status>failed</status>, and on any agent that was spawned, never stopped, and has been silent past module_config.orphan_watch.stale_minutes. THE TWO ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF CLAIM and the alert says which is which: the first is REPORTED by the harness, the second INFERRED from silence. REQUIRES failure_capture: it runs below that gate because SubagentStop records are what failure_capture writes, and reconciling against records nothing was writing would call every finished agent an orphan. failure_capture off = orphan_watch inert.

repos.$comment: Per-repo overrides keyed by the 'owner/name' slug of the ORIGIN REMOTE. The slug is resolved from the hook payload's cwd - walk up for .git, read the origin url out of its config - because payload.workspace does NOT exist in any hook event; it is built only for the status line. Until this was fixed every hook resolved the repo to null and nothing in this block applied to anything. Keys are matched case-insensitively. Only the modules listed under a repo are overridden; everything else falls through to the global defaults above. Example: "LEAPWare-Software/example-repo": { "modules": { "docs_coupling": false } }

thresholds.$ratelimit_comment: Read by ~/.claude/statusline.ps1, which is the only process that receives rate_limits at all. There is no ratelimit_escalation module and there cannot be - it was removed on 30 July 2026 because no hook is given the data; see $status.$removed_blocked_comment and docs/modules.md. WHAT THESE TWO NUMBERS ACTUALLY DRIVE, corrected on 3 August 2026: the SECOND ROW only - whether the 'approaching limit' / 'land all work' advisory appears, which of the two texts it takes and which colour it is printed in. They do NOT colour the percentage on row 1. That colour comes from Heat(), which holds three fixed band edges at 50/75/90 and reads no configuration at all, so on the shipped defaults a rate limit turns red at 90 while the advisory still says 'approaching' until 92. The sentence here used to say these numbers drove 'the status line's colouring', and an operator who lowered them and watched the figure's colour saw nothing change.
thresholds.$context_comment: The same distinction as $ratelimit_comment, for the ctx segment: these two decide the advisory on row 2 and not the colour of the figure on row 1. A configured 0 is honoured and means 'always' - it used to be discarded as falsy - and a value that is not a number is named on the advisory row and the built-in below is used instead of it, rather than being swapped in silently. /lw-watchtower:doctor validates nothing under thresholds.

module_config.$comment: Per-module tuning, read through Get-LwgModuleOption. Separate from `thresholds`, which is only the two numeric pressure groups. Every key here is optional: the code carries the same defaults, so deleting this block changes nothing.

context_pressure.$comment: context_window is NOT in any hook payload, so occupancy is recomputed from the transcript's last assistant usage block using the CLI's own formula: round((input + cache_creation + cache_read) / window * 100). The one number that genuinely cannot be observed is the WINDOW SIZE - it depends on account entitlements. The CLI only ever picks 200000 or 1000000, so: an entry below wins; else a model id tagged [1m] is 1000000; else a model previously SEEN holding more than 200000 tokens is proven to be 1000000 (recorded in context_windows.json in the state dir, self-correcting after one turn); else 200000 is assumed and the advisory says so. If occupancy ever exceeds the assumed window the percentage is suppressed entirely rather than reported as a false 100%. Add a model here if you would rather not rely on the fallbacks.
context_pressure.$window_tokens_comment: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and it must ship empty. An entry here is the HIGHEST-trust source and wins outright over the [1m] tag, over the observed-proof rule and over the default - which is correct for an operator stating a fact about their own account, and wrong for a value shipped to every install, because the window depends on ACCOUNT ENTITLEMENT and no single number is true for every reader. A hardcoded 1000000 on a 200k-entitled account makes context_pressure report occupancy at one fifth of the truth and stay silent straight through a compaction, with the entry suppressing the very fallbacks that would have self-corrected it. Empty, the chain runs: [1m] tag, else a window PROVEN by having been seen holding more than 200k tokens (persisted in context_windows.json, self-correcting after one turn), else 200k assumed and the advisory says so. Add your own model here only if you would rather not rely on that chain; an absent or empty block is read the same way, so deleting it changes nothing.

git_hygiene.$comment: The ONLY module allowed to spawn a subprocess, and it does so on Stop only - never per render and never on PreToolUse, so it cannot delay or hang a tool call. Outside a git repo it spawns nothing at all. The common case is one `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch`, which answers dirty / detached / ahead / behind together; a second `git rev-list` runs only on a branch with no upstream. A git command that times out, is missing or exits nonzero is reported as UNKNOWN - never as a clean tree. timeout_ms bounds each git call, gh_timeout_ms the one optional network call. use_gh false disables the open-PR check entirely; when true it still only runs where it can matter (unpushed work on a non-default branch) and is asked at most once per branch head per session. default_branches is the fallback used when refs/remotes/origin/HEAD is absent, which is normal in a repo that was created rather than cloned.

send_liveness_gate.$comment: stale_minutes divides 'presumed running' from 'dead mid-flight' for a recipient with no SubagentStop record. Default 15, floor 1, and the default sits ABOVE the 10-minute Bash tool ceiling on purpose: an agent inside one long tool call writes nothing to its transcript for the length of the call, and a threshold under that ceiling would refuse sends to agents that are merely busy. The measured dead recipient had been silent 28m45s.

orphan_watch.$comment: Same number, same reasoning, applied to the transcript reconciliation instead of the send path. The two are separate knobs deliberately: an operator can make the alert patient while keeping the gate strict, or the reverse. THIS IS THE ONLY THRESHOLD, and a death the HARNESS has named does not serve it at all - see $removed_error_stale_comment.
orphan_watch.$removed_error_stale_comment: error_stale_minutes WAS a second, five-minute threshold for a transcript whose last record was an isApiErrorMessage, on the reasoning that a stated cause need not wait out inferred silence, with rate_limit and 529 excluded as back-pressure. IT WAS REMOVED ON 10 AUGUST 2026 BECAUSE IT WAS MEASURED REPORTING A LIVE AGENT DEAD, and the removal is recorded here rather than left to be inferred from an absence. Re-derived over 1,050 transcripts, all four mid-file API errors RECOVERED, with gaps 25.4s, 93.8s, 3,824.0s and 4,011.2s. The 4,011.2s one is error 'server_error' with NO apiErrorStatus and no '529' or 'Overloaded' anywhere in its text, so it fell through the class exclusion onto the five-minute path and would have been alerted as DIED while it went on working for another 62 minutes - one false positive in four. The threshold cannot be raised to fix it either: the longest live recovery is 66.85 MINUTES, longer than the 15-minute silence rule it existed to beat, so it bought nothing. What replaces it is better on both axes - the harness's own <status>failed</status> task-notification in the parent transcript, which is terminal by construction because a recovering agent is never given one, and which is believed with NO threshold at all. DO NOT REINTRODUCE A THRESHOLD KEYED ON TRANSCRIPT PROSE: the classifier failed because it substring-matched English the API is free to reword.

docs_coupling.$comment: A path is doc, source, or neither; doc wins. Directories match on a whole path SEGMENT, so 'docs' does not match 'src/docsify'. Data and config files (.json, .yaml, .toml, lockfiles) are deliberately in neither bucket - counting lockfile churn as a source change is how this module would become noise. Only edits made through Write/Edit/NotebookEdit are recorded; a file rewritten by a shell command is invisible.
